key_insight: Adding 1 wt.% CeO2 or La2O3 to HVOF-sprayed WC–12Co reduced porosity and refined grains, with CeO2 delivering the lowest friction and La2O3 the lowest wear rate.
engineering_relevance: Rare-earth oxide reinforcement offers a route to harder, more wear-resistant WC–12Co coatings without compromising bond strength.
method: Deposit unreinforced and CeO2- or La2O3-reinforced WC–12Co coatings using HVOF.
Compare microstructure, phase composition, microhardness, bond strength, abrasive wear, and friction.
Examine worn surfaces using scanning electron microscopy.
evidence_signal: At 1 wt.% reinforcement, CeO2 and La2O3 increased microhardness by 6% and 4%, respectively; La2O3 achieved a minimum wear rate of 3.5 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), while CeO2 achieved a minimum friction coefficient of 0.4.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or long-term service performance, limiting direct transfer of these results to component design.
paper_title: EFFECT OF CEO2 AND LA2O3 REINFORCEMENTS ON MECHANICAL, TRIBOLOGICAL AND MICROSTRUCTURAL PROPERTIES OF WC–12CO COATING BY HIGH-VELOCITY OXYGEN FUEL DEPOSITION TECHNIQUE
